name: connectors
title: Connectors
summary: People connect their accounts on Google, Microsoft, GitHub, GitLab, Notion, HubSpot, Salesforce and Zoom once and every feature uses them as that person, with incremental consent and workspace policy; the assistant also reaches external MCP servers.

env.name: CONNECTORS_ENCRYPTION_KEY
env.doc: 32 random bytes (base64 or 64 hex characters) sealing users' tokens with AES-256-GCM. Development falls back to a public, logged development key.

env.name: CONNECTORS_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS
env.doc: The key before a rotation: still opens values sealed with it while a job re-seals them with CONNECTORS_ENCRYPTION_KEY. Remove it after the log says it can be removed.

env.name: CONNECTORS_ALLOW_CUSTOM
env.doc: Let users add their own MCP servers by URL (up to 10 each); their tool annotations aren't trusted, so every tool counts as a change.

env.name: CONNECTORS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORKS
env.doc: Allow connector servers on loopback and private addresses (local test servers). Development only; link-local and cloud metadata addresses stay blocked.

env.name: CONNECTORS_TOOL_CACHE_TTL
env.doc: How long each connection's tool list is kept before the server is asked again.

env.name: CONNECTORS_TOOL_TIMEOUT
env.doc: Longest a remote tool call may run (5s to 2m).

env.name: CONNECTORS_DEV_PROVIDER_URLS
env.doc: Development only: point platforms at local mocks, as provider=http://127.0.0.1:port pairs separated by commas; each platform URL becomes <mock>/<original host><path>. Refused outside development.

env.name: GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID
env.doc: Google OAuth client ID for sign-in. Unset: Google shows Not set up.

env.name: GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET
env.doc: Google OAuth client secret (set together with GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID).

env.name: MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID
env.doc: Microsoft (Entra ID) OAuth client ID for sign-in. Unset: Microsoft shows Not set up.

env.name: MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET
env.doc: Microsoft (Entra ID) OAuth client secret (set together with MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID).

env.name: MICROSOFT_TENANT
env.doc: Entra tenant for sign-in: common (any work or personal account), organizations, consumers, or one tenant id/domain.

env.name: GITHUB_CLIENT_ID
env.doc: GitHub (OAuth App) OAuth client ID for sign-in. Unset: GitHub shows Not set up (personal tokens still work).

env.name: GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET
env.doc: GitHub (OAuth App) OAuth client secret (set together with GITHUB_CLIENT_ID).

env.name: GITLAB_CLIENT_ID
env.doc: GitLab OAuth client ID for sign-in. Unset: GitLab shows Not set up (personal tokens still work).

env.name: GITLAB_CLIENT_SECRET
env.doc: GitLab OAuth client secret (set together with GITLAB_CLIENT_ID).

env.name: GITLAB_BASE_URL
env.doc: GitLab instance sign-in uses (a self-managed instance's address, or gitlab.com). Personal tokens may name any instance.

env.name: NOTION_CLIENT_ID
env.doc: Notion (public integration) OAuth client ID for sign-in. Unset: Notion shows Not set up (personal tokens still work).

env.name: NOTION_CLIENT_SECRET
env.doc: Notion (public integration) OAuth client secret (set together with NOTION_CLIENT_ID).

env.name: HUBSPOT_CLIENT_ID
env.doc: HubSpot OAuth client ID for sign-in. Unset: HubSpot shows Not set up (personal tokens still work).

env.name: HUBSPOT_CLIENT_SECRET
env.doc: HubSpot OAuth client secret (set together with HUBSPOT_CLIENT_ID).

env.name: SALESFORCE_CLIENT_ID
env.doc: Salesforce (connected app) OAuth client ID for sign-in. Unset: Salesforce shows Not set up.

env.name: SALESFORCE_CLIENT_SECRET
env.doc: Salesforce (connected app) OAuth client secret (set together with SALESFORCE_CLIENT_ID).

env.name: SALESFORCE_LOGIN_URL
env.doc: Salesforce login host: login.salesforce.com, test.salesforce.com (sandboxes) or your My Domain.

env.name: ZOOM_CLIENT_ID
env.doc: Zoom (general app) OAuth client ID for sign-in. Unset: Zoom shows Not set up.

env.name: ZOOM_CLIENT_SECRET
env.doc: Zoom (general app) OAuth client secret (set together with ZOOM_CLIENT_ID).

env.name: GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET
env.doc: Secret of GitHub webhooks sent to /webhooks/connectors/github (X-Hub-Signature-256). Unset: refused.

env.name: GITLAB_WEBHOOK_SECRET
env.doc: Secret token of GitLab webhooks sent to /webhooks/connectors/gitlab (X-Gitlab-Token). Unset: refused.

env.name: NOTION_WEBHOOK_SECRET
env.doc: Verification token of the Notion webhook subscription (X-Notion-Signature). Unset: refused.

env.name: ZOOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET
env.doc: Secret token of the Zoom app's event subscription (x-zm-signature, URL validation). Unset: refused.

env.name: GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_TOKEN
env.doc: Channel token features set on Google Drive/Calendar watches (X-Goog-Channel-Token). Unset: refused.

env.name: MICROSOFT_WEBHOOK_CLIENT_STATE
env.doc: clientState features set on Microsoft Graph subscriptions. Unset: refused.

stitch: Set CONNECTORS_ENCRYPTION_KEY (openssl rand -base64 32) in every non-development environment; keep the old key in CONNECTORS_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS while rotating, and remove it only after the log line "CONNECTORS_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS can be removed".

Make PUBLIC_API_URL the public https address of the API: authorization servers redirect to <PUBLIC_API_URL>/v1/connectors/oauth/callback, and servers that support Client ID Metadata Documents fetch <PUBLIC_API_URL>/v1/connectors/oauth/client-metadata.json.
Curate the catalog in Admin → Connectors: use Check to see whether a service registers itself or needs a client ID registered with it (redirect URL above), and decide each connector's Changes policy.
Decide CONNECTORS_ALLOW_CUSTOM: leave it off unless people should add arbitrary MCP servers.
Install the assistant feature (1.1.0 or later) so connected tools reach it; without it, connections have no consumer.

Name each connected service as a processor in the privacy policy only if your company operates it; otherwise say that the assistant sends the user's requests to services they connect, and their results to the AI provider.
If the mobile app's scheme changes, update mobileReturnURL in backend/internal/connectors/connectors.go and RETURN_URL in mobile/src/features/connectors/ConnectionsScreen.tsx together.

Register an OAuth app with each platform you want people to sign in to (the consent screen shows its name), with redirect URL <PUBLIC_API_URL>/v1/connectors/oauth/callback, and set its <PLATFORM>_CLIENT_ID and _SECRET. Admin → Connectors → Platforms shows what is missing. GitHub, GitLab, Notion and HubSpot also take personal tokens without any setup.
Request verification of sensitive scopes where the platform requires it before launch (Google restricted/sensitive scopes such as Drive, Microsoft admin consent for org-wide permissions).

Decide each workspace's default connection policy (Settings → Connection policy; admins), and name the platforms people may connect in the privacy policy (data stays on the platform and is read live with the person's own token).
